utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. Case Number IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam. Mr. Brdjanin, can you follow in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please be seated. And Madam Korner, appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Animated conversation with Ms. Gustin about exhibits. It's Joanna Korner, Ann Sutherland, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman, with David Cunningham, and Aleksandar Vujic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you and good afternoon to you. Any preliminaries before we proceed? Right. Usher, thank you. As I said, we will need to stop just before 5.00. So Madam Registrar, if you could think between now and when we should have a break, when we should have a break, if we could have just one break, it would be better.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I suggest, why don't we break at 20 minutes to 4.00, until 4.00, and then 4.00 until 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's agreeable to you, I understand, Mr. Ackerman, because I did not hear you complain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I almost never complain about anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, I know. Everyone talks about it actually. Mr. Ackerman's synonymous with no complaints. Mr. Radic is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You reckon you need how long, Mr. Ackerman? Another hour? Hour and a half?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm going to try for an hour, Judge. The problem is without the ability to use something like Sanction, it's going to be tedious just dealing with documents, dragging them back and forth. But we're working on it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I thought there were no complaints.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No, that wasn't a complaint. That was just answering His Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But to think of it, for two years, he never used it and it never was a problem, and that today that he cannot use it, it has become a problem. Mr. Radic, good afternoon to you. We are proceeding with your testimony today. May I remind you that you are testifying under oath and on the basis of the solemn declaration, in other words, that you entered yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Am I supposed to stand up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, you are a professional man, so I don't need to waste my words. You are under oath. You are going to continue testifying. Mr. Ackerman will proceed with his direct. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Ackerman: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Radic. Welcome back.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we stopped yesterday, we were dealing with the subject of dismissals and the June 22nd, 1992 decision of the ARK Crisis Staff in that regard. What I want to do now is look at some documents which indicate that a municipality or two may have paid some attention to that document. I just want you to notice them. If you look at first of all P1879. Well, that's nowhere near the document that I was looking for. P1879 should be a completely different document. I think there's another one, the same document is also P255, if that helps. I think it has got two different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 255 we saw yesterday, and that's the document, the decision of the ARK Crisis Staff purportedly signed by Radoslav Brdjanin. And the witness said he wouldn't -- couldn't recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That's not the one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that is 255.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. 1879 is the one we need.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, you should have a document dated 25 June 1992, three days after the 22 June ARK Crisis Staff document, which is a document directed to the ARK Crisis Staff regarding implementation of the 22 June order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and if I may add at this point, this is why you got confused with P255, because decision number 03-531/92 is precisely the decision that is reported in Exhibit 255.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So let's move ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you'll look at this, the crisis staff in Petrovac is telling the crisis staff of the autonomous region that they have implemented that 22 June decision. If you look, for instance, going down to a paragraph after the indented paragraphs, it says: "Speaking about the employees of Serb nationality..." Do you see that? Do you see the part I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we go on, I wonder if we could ask whether Mr. Radic has ever seen this document. Because if he hasn't, then I'm not sure how he's supposed to be able to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, he can still comment on it because he is seeing it now. But your question is very pertinent. Did you see this document before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is the first time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And are you in a position to comment on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is too short a time for me to on it. The only thing I can see is the people of non-Serb ethnicity were dismissed from the public security station as well as employees of the municipal assembly. All of them in the administration but one. As far as the Serb workers are concerned, according to our knowledge from -- as for the employees of the Serb ethnicity, according to our information, in all the public enterprises and companies, people have already been sacked from these jobs cited in item 1 of the decision. All the employees cited in paragraph 3, item 1. As for the units of the Serb -- BiH Serb Republic Army, the steps set by AR Krajina Crisis Staff are in the stage of being implemented. Since taking into account that not all staff could be dismissed before the necessary takeover could be carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Radic, if you sit here and read all these documents to us, you'll be here until Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Until Friday of next week. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just had one question about this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You tell me when to stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Stop. From now on, when I show you a document, wait for me to ask you a question about it, and I will point you to the part of it that I'm interested in. Feel free, however, to read the document any time you feel it's necessary for you to do so. But don't read us to us, that just taxes the interpreters unnecessarily, because we do have translations of all these documents. The only part of this one that I'm interested in is that paragraph that reads: "Speaking about employees of Serb nationality, all the employees cited in paragraph 3, item 1 of the decision have already been sacked from those jobs cited in item 1 in all public enterprises and institutions." In other words, even though Petrovac says that what they're doing is complying with that June 22nd decision, they are pointing out that they already had sacked all those people before that decision even came out. Correct?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Rajko Novakovic, the signatory of this document, he is the president of the Municipal Assembly of Petrovac. So he must have done this even before he received this instruction from the crisis staff. However, there's one confusing thing here in the last paragraph. He informs that the crisis staff has dismissed soldiers, members of the army. I don't know where this authority comes from. How could he also dismiss soldiers? Because the dismissals of soldiers could only be done by the army command and not any civilian organ of authority. In this case, the president of the Municipal Assembly of Petrovac. Unfortunately, you will not be able to get his statement because he was killed in the early days of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to look now at the next document. It's P1837.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that this document is not very legible. It's very hard for me to read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm -- the only thing I'm really interested in with regard to this document is that it is a document from Petrovac, that it's dated 29 June 1992, that it refers to the 22 decision -- 22 June decision of the ARK Crisis Staff, and it actually grants leave without pay to a worker by the name of Senada Mehdin who apparently was laid off in accordance with the ARK Crisis Staff decision. I don't know if you can see that from the illegible copy you've got, but I tell you that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What was your question, sir?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just -- I just wanted you to see the document, and in preparation for some additional questions I will ask you later, to know that this is another case where there was at least some implementation of the 22 June crisis staff decision. We can just go on to the next document now. It's DB312. This document, DB312, you might be familiar with, and what I'd like you to do is look at it and tell me if you are familiar with it and if you recall seeing it before.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bosko Lukic. I don't know. I've never seen this before. It says: "Penal and correctional facility." This is the penal and correctional facility which was under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are a state institution of special state importance, and the flow of information could go from there towards the -- those people who were detained. "We hereby informed you that we have carried out our obligation as ordered in the decision of the AR Autonomous Region of Krajina and we have employed the" --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please don't read the document, please.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the document for the first time. I really don't know what your question is going to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you want to go ahead and read it, but don't do it outloud because that makes the translators translate it and we have a translation. If you want to sit there and read it to yourself, feel free. I wouldn't mind that at all. The thing I'm interested in is if you look right underneath the date, it says that it's addressed to the president of the Banja Luka Municipal Crisis Staff, which I think, on 26 June 1992, was probably you. And my question is: Did you receive this document or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why this was sent to me when it says here that this penal and correctional facility is an institution of exceptional public importance, and it was under the direct authority of the Ministry of the Interior. Because here, he says in the first paragraph: "We hereby inform you that we have carried out our obligations as ordered in the decision of the AR Krajina Crisis Staff." This was just information for our reference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But what it does indicate that this is another situation where that 22 June decision was actually implemented, wasn't it, apparently?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it transpires from this that this was the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I'd like you to look at P1290. Now, I think you've seen this one. I think you saw it a couple of days ago. I believe I showed it to you. You might remember. That doesn't look like the document I'm interested in. Can I see what you've got there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Usher, let's economise on time. Take mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's the same thing. All right. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's very brief, so you can read it to yourself very quickly. And I think I showed it to you the other day.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document again refers to that 22 June 1992 decision of the ARK Crisis Staff. And it says it's being forwarded for implementation. But it doesn't indicate anywhere, does it, where it's being forwarded?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know just from your own knowledge whether it actually was forwarded to anybody and implemented in Prijedor in any degree at all?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It says here that the Municipality of Prijedor or its crisis staff is the one that is forwarding it. And the signatory is Dr. Milomir Stakic. There's no addressee. There is no list of addressees, so it is very difficult for me to even assume who the addressees were, who this document was sent to. It must have been somebody in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Prijedor was a municipality that was particularly obedient to the ARK Crisis Staff? Were they a municipality that always did what the ARK Crisis Staff suggested?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you have a document where it says very clearly that the decisions of the Crisis Staff of the AR Krajina do not have to be implemented in Prijedor. You must have a document of that nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at P1268. The decision that I need you to look at is at decision number 119. And I'm going to help you with the page number here in just a second, if I can. Yes, if you look at -- up at the top you'll see the number 0017800. If you find what is page 800, then you'll find decision 119 at the bottom of that page.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is here, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that's a decision of 25 June 1992, just three days after the decision of the ARK Crisis Staff that we have been talking about. Isn't it?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to this decision at the very top of the page?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's number 119 at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And that's the one you were referring to when you said that there was -- you knew there was such a decision from Prijedor. Correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I remembered it. And it wasn't binding for me. I read it, and it was clear to me that the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality would not observe any enactments adopted by the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina until such time as the Assembly of AR Krajina has elected all members of the government and so on and so forth. So this was not binding for the government or for the implementation of any government decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Radic, what I'm going to do now may be easy to do, or it may be hard. I hope it's easy. I have a very large number of documents that I want you to look at just very briefly. And each one of them, I believe, is a Prijedor decision dismissing someone from their employment. And the Registrar going to have to be really helpful with regard to this. We need Documents P1173 through 1176. 1173, 74, 75, 76, 78, 78, and then 85 and 87 and 88 and 89 and 91 and 99. And 1201 and 1205. And then DB313 and 314. Now, there's a lot of paper there, Mr. Radic, and all in the world I want you to do is look at each of those and confirm for the Trial Chamber that they are Prijedor-ordered dismissals, all of which preceded the June 22nd decision of the ARK Crisis Staff. And once you've done that, then I have an additional question to ask you about.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about these first two documents. They refer to the people that I know, Milenko Djukanovic, Mirko Savic, his deputy. Miroslav who was with Cikota, Topic Ranko was the one who replaced him. But here, let me just have a look. The date is the 2nd of May, 1992. Therefore, before that time. This one is in English. Do you have it in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turn it over to the other side. It's probably --

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is also in English. It refers to Mirko Brkic and Savic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, usher, which document does he have in front of him and let's keep it one document at a time, please. Mr. Radic, which document do you have in front of you? Can I have the number, exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2150 or the one at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He has got P1173. We start with that one. 1173. Take them all in your hand, usher, please, and find P1173. Mr. Ackerman, 1173, 1174.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Then 1185.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 85 I don't have. I have 1186. 1187. 1185 I have as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: There should be 1201 and 1205, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have them all usher? Okay. Let's start with 1173, please. Mr. Radic, do you have Exhibit P1173 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It should refer to Milenko Djukanovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. Djukanovic, yes, yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And the date on that one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Djukanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The 2nd May. Yes, that's it. Make sure that he has -- okay, but he said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The next one should be 1174, Miroslav Turnsek.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1174. Are you going to put one cumulative, all-encompassing question or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: At the end, when he has seen all the documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Ranko Topic. Yes. Next.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Next should be 1174 -- 75.

utterances.text: And that one should be Idriz Jakupovic, and it should be the 2nd of May. Right? Do you have that one, Mr. Radic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you have it, Mr. Radic?

utterances.text: Prijedor, Nikola Saric, yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that one is 5 May 1992

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hilmija.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1188. That should be Vahid Seric, 5 May?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vahid Seric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one is 1189, that should be Jasminka Hadzibegovic?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next one should be 1191, Dzemal Sefer, 7 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dzemal Sefer, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And 1199 is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But I don't see it on my list. Yes, here it is. There it is.

utterances.text: 313 is -- do you have it, usher? It's about Izet Mehmedagic and Slobodan Radulovic.

utterances.speaker: PREDRAG RADIC [Resumed]
